diagnosis_explanation: Your knee has a problem with wear and tear. This is called osteoarthritis. It can cause pain and make it hard to move.
medication_rationale:
Mirapex:
This medicine helps your body move more easily. It can help with stiffness. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is often mild. Call your doctor if you feel very tired. Also call if you get nausea or vomiting.

Ibuprofen:
This medicine reduces pain and swelling in your knee. It is an anti-inflammatory. You may notice your stomach feels upset. Taking it with food can help. Call your doctor if you see black or tarry stools. Also call if you get severe stomach pain.

Ambien:
This medicine helps you fall asleep. It is for short-term use. You may feel drowsy the next day. Do not drive or do tasks needing alertness. Call your doctor if you do things like sleepwalk or eat while asleep. You do not remember these actions.

Percocet:
This medicine is a strong pain reliever. It is for severe pain. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. Constipation is also common. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you feel very confused.

Coumadin:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. It makes your blood flow more smoothly. You may bruise or bleed more easily. This is expected. Call your doctor right away if you bleed a lot. Also call if you notice blood in your urine or stool.
Important: Do not stop taking this medicine without calling your doctor first.
Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and have some pain in your knee.
- Keep your knee clean and dry.
- Do not put any weight on your right leg.
- Use your walker or crutches for all walking.
- Follow your physical therapist's instructions carefully.
- Do not bend your knee more than 90 degrees.
- Your goal this week is to do your exercises every day.
- Call your doctor if your pain gets much worse or is not controlled.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain should start to get a little better.
- You may feel a little more energy each day.
- Continue to use your walker or crutches for support.
- You can start putting a little weight on your right leg.
- Keep bending your knee gently as instructed by therapy.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little more inside your home.
- Call your doctor if you see any redness or swelling around your knee.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel less pain and more comfort.
- You can start to walk with one crutch or a cane.
- Continue with your physical therapy exercises.
- Do not push yourself too hard; listen to your body.
- Your goal this week is to walk a short distance outside.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101 degrees Fahrenheit.

**Week 4:**
- You will likely have more energy and less pain.
- You may be able to walk without a cane or crutches.
- Continue all prescribed exercises to build strength.
- You can start to do light household chores.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes at a time.
- Call your doctor if you notice any sudden swelling or pain in your calf.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your knee will feel better over the next few months.
- Keep up with your physical therapy exercises.
- Continue to walk regularly to build strength.
- Follow your doctor's advice for long-term recovery.
- Most people return to normal activities in about 3 to 6 months.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Knee pain is not better: Ask about pain relief options.
- Knee swelling is worse: Your doctor can check the joint.
- Trouble walking or moving: Discuss ways to improve motion.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can explain doses.
